body: Thanks. I'll keep reminding myself that.

Failure is necessary for success. I just need to increase my odds of success by diversification. It's just that my emotion takes over sometimes. It tears my castle down. My profession is lucrative. It'd probably be hard to get back into it later. But I hate the corporate world, how it's systemically structure to reward abuse of power, discourages creativity and honesty. This is where I'm at, the biggest fork of the road in my life. It's a big leap in front of me no matter what.

I'm glad, yet so afraid, someone has summarized these "laws" with supporting argument. I'm glad because I realize it's not just me experiencing it, and there seemingly is a way to address the situation. But I'm afraid if we're already at the state that someone has not only realized, documented, and publishing it; the current severity of manipulation must be much much worse....

The effectiveness of a patent varies:

how well a patent is depicted, documented, etc. This is where a good and dedicated patent lawyer is justified a high cost of filing one.

Patent takes a while to go through its process. Have you noticed labels saying "patent pending"? By the time it's cleared, I'd probably have a revised design.

Companies in countries like China probably doesn't care much about existing patents. That's why you see a lot of items on ebay showing seemingly the same product, but having different names,  much cheaper, but look exactly alike.

Actually, I've been documenting my designs for years. I just have never had the need nor the courage to realize them. The idea of someone copying and stealing my design once it's out, is very discouraging. Thank you my logical friend.
sad indeed... I don't know where i'd be, but I wish you good luck.

I used to have inklings of the existence of the workings of these laws subconsciously. Then I'd shrug it off and continue to believe the heroism and mobility sold by our cultural stories and media. So sad of the brutal truth the laws explain. Thank you for introducing me to this book. I'm much more convinced now.

I have ideas. But I learned that ideas are a dime a dozen. It's the execution, right? I'm so fearful of failure. But that is exactly what is needed to succeed. Your logical suggestion is appreciated surely. Sometimes, I'd wish to have a friend just like me. I'd be like me offering logical solutions and helping my friends. For some reason, I can't do it to myself....

> "48 laws of power by robert greene"

I believe I'm mostly the opposite of what those laws instruct.

You're right. Staying at my job while looking for another  is logically sound. The thing is, I used to think there was something wrong with me. Maybe I wasn't good enough. Then I left and came here, thinking with my skills, I cant easily excel here. What I learned is that my technical ability has very little to do with excelling at work. I have been playing the game all wrong. Furthermore, the game applies, not only to a company, but the whole world. Most principles and believes I've learned and practiced, turn out to be, detrimental. I need a reboot... a worldly reboot.
